prompt: In the last century, the first man to walk on the moon said it was "a giant leap for mankind”. However, some people think it has made little difference to our daily lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Opinions are divided on whether the saying "a giant leap for mankind" of the first walking to the moon could make any difference to our daily lives. From my perspective, I totally agree with the positive side for the following reasons.

The chief excuse for my stance is that such a first step on the moon heralds humanity's power and motivates relentless effort to develop. In contrast to the past, when mankind was restricted by the earth itself, had no tools to reach the skies, and deemed planets and stars almost unfathomable, the journey to the moon broke our previous limits and showcased our strength in exploring and deciphering the unknown. This effort also requires rich, rare resources, a high budget, extensive training, creativity, and ultimately, humans' indomitable spirit for scientific thrive. The satisfying result emerging at the expense of these prices is indeed precious, a testament to meritocracy, where sacrifices can produce miracles at the end. Even after decades of that event, many, especially people working in astronomy, are still inspired and motivated to do tasks with challenges ahead, carrying a mindset of equivalent exchange - values are not created by nothing.

Equally noticeable for my justification is that the first walk on the moon has set the foundation for new occupations and innovations. This is illustrated clearly in sectors like aerospace, commercial space flights (SpaceX or Blue Origin companies), medical tech, and the advanced image processing profession. Meanwhile, to make the moon landing possible, NASA had to invent or drastically improve materials and systems. These breakthroughs transitioned into commercial products we rely on today. The Apollo Guidance Computer pioneered the use of unproven integrated circuits to save weight, which helped spur the microchip revolution, leading to modern laptops, smartphones, and digital devices. Another case is that multi-layer reflective mylar insulation sheets were engineered to protect astronauts from extreme radiation and heat.These sheets were later packaged into lightweight emergency kits, marathon running wraps, and commercial home insulation. Such progress is undeniably impactful, changing our daily lives for the better convenience.

In conclusion, I fervently agree with the astronaut's highlight of the integral role of the travel to the moon. With its inspiration and practical applications to daily lives, it truly deserves the title of "one giant leap for mankind".
